title: Suspected Melanoma: Skin Lesion Assessment and Dermatology Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with a pigmented skin lesion suspected to be melanoma: weighted 7-point checklist, dermoscopy, suspected cancer pathway referral, excision, staging with computed tomography (CT) and treatment overview.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG14 names systemic drugs (encorafenib with binimetinib, dabrafenib with trametinib, nivolumab, ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, dacarbazine) and topical imiquimod without doses; no dosing source was opened for these specialist oncology medicines.
NICE NG12 states no timeframe for melanoma referral in the text opened.
The 2 mm excision biopsy margin and the 7-point checklist features beyond those quoted were not opened in primary form.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Melanoma arises from melanocytes and can metastasise to lymph nodes and distant sites. NICE recommends dermoscopy, carried out by trained healthcare professionals, to assess pigmented skin lesions. Stage determines excision margin, sentinel lymph node biopsy, imaging and systemic therapy. BRAF V600 mutation status guides targeted therapy in advanced disease.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Stable, symmetric, uniform colour; atypical lesions can be compared with baseline photographs at 3 months.
Managed as melanoma when malignant potential is uncertain.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess the lesion
actions: Apply the weighted 7-point checklist and dermoscopy by trained staff.
Compare atypical lesions not needing excision with baseline photographs at 3 months.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
actions: Refer if the score is 3 or more or dermoscopy suggests melanoma.

clinicalManagement.title: Excise and stage
actions: Wide excision margin: stage 0 at least 0.5 cm; stage I 1 cm; stage II 2 cm.
Stage with CT as above; no imaging or sentinel biopsy for stage IA.

clinicalManagement.title: Follow-up
actions: Stage IA: follow-up for 1 year. Stages IB to IV: 5 years.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG14 names topical imiquimod for stage 0 melanoma and systemic therapies for stage IV or unresectable stage III disease (encorafenib plus binimetinib, dabrafenib plus trametinib, nivolumab, ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, dacarbazine) but gives no doses. These are specialist oncology prescriptions decided by the multidisciplinary team under the hospital oncology protocol. Primary care assessment and referral need no medicine.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Weighted 7-point checklist score of 3 or more, or dermoscopy suggesting melanoma.
Change in size, irregular shape, irregular colour.
Largest diameter 7 mm or more, inflammation, oozing, change in sensation.
